previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, morbid obesity, and a history of multiple line infections was admitted after developing hypotension following hemodialysis. She presented with symptoms of infection, including nausea, vomiting, and a productive cough, and was found to be in septic shock with Klebsiella bacteremia. Imaging revealed choledocholithiasis and a dilated common bile duct, leading to a diagnosis of cholangitis. She was intubated for hypercarbic respiratory failure and managed in the ICU with vasopressors, antibiotics, and a percutaneous biliary drain. Once stable, she underwent ERCP with stone extraction and biliary stent placement. A left lower extremity DVT was identified near her dialysis catheter, requiring anticoagulation with a heparin bridge to Coumadin. She also developed pruritus, likely due to a reaction to bleached sheets, which resolved with intervention. Her hospital course was prolonged but successful, with resolution of infection and stabilization of her condition. She was discharged to extended care with plans to return for stent removal and ongoing management of her anticoagulation, dialysis, and comorbidities.

Brief Hospital Course:
PRIMARY REASON FOR HOSPITALIZATION:
___ with history of DMII, PAH, OSA, ESRD on HD, and recent 
admission for sepsis secondary to cholangitis, complicated by 
DVT at site of femoral dialysis line, admitted with low grade 
fevers at nursing home. 

ACTIVE DIAGNOSES:
# DVT: Patient had DVT on last admission around site of HD 
catheter in femoral vein.  She is on warfarin for 
anticoagulation.  Her INR on admission was subtherapeutic and 
dangerous in the setting of a known DVT.  Repeat b/l ___ showed 
resolving clot burden in right lower extremity (some flow around 
clots) and no DVT in left lower extremity.  Patient's warfarin 
regimen was adjusted until she became therapeutic.  At the time 
of discharge, INR was 2.3.  

# Fever: Patient was having low grade fevers during last 
hospitalization, which was attributed to DVT. She was afebrile 
at time of discharge, but was noted at rehab facility to be 
febrile yesterday to 100.2.  Differential for fevers includes HD 
catheter line infection, pneumonia, and bacteremia.  At the time 
of recent discharge, femoral dialysis line was noted to be 
draining ___ discharge.  Swabs were sent for culture 
and were negative for growth.  On exam today, dialysis site 
looks clean and intact, with no discharge or erythema. CXR in ED 
was negative for pneumonia, and patient received levofloxacin 
750 mg and ciprofloxacin in ED for concern for pneumonia. This 
was not continued on the floor, as there was no evidence of 
infection.  Blood cultures were drawn in the ED and on the 
floor, and were all negative by the time of discharge.  Since 
admission, patient has been afebrile (highest temperature was 
99.1) and does not have a leukocytosis.  

# Decreased appetite: Patient has had decreased appetite over 
past several days, coinciding with severe constipation.  She 
denies nausea/vomiting.  Tonight, she felt quite hungry after 
not eating in the ED and tolerated dinner well.  Abdominal exam 
was benign and not concerning for obstruction.  Diffusely and 
mildly tender, especially in LLQ, which may be consistent with 
constipation.  Since admission, patient has had voracious 
appetite and eaten all meals, so appetite appears back to 
baseline.  On ___, had a large bowel movement after 
suppository so abdominal distension is much improved.  Patient 
was given another suppository and had another bowel movement 
prior to discharge.

# ESRD on HD: Patient has been receiving dialysis per 
nephrology; is on a ___ schedule.  Patient appears fairly 
euvolemic with no crackles and only trace peripheral edema.  Her 
electrolytes were monitored at HD and she was continued on 
sevelamer and nephrocaps.

#. Anemia: Hct 24.7 on admission, which is a little lower than 
recent baseline of 27.  Anemia is macrocytic to 105 with widened 
RDW, so may have a microcytic component as well.  Fe studies 
also showed mild iron deficiency and ACD.  She was continued on 
iron and epo with HD.  She was continued on folic acid 
supplementation
on the floor

#. HTN/Vascular: Patient was recently discharged off of 
antihypertensives due to hypotension during last admission.  
Currently, patient is normotensive in the systolic 100s-130s off 
all blood pressure medications.  Midodrine, which was carried 
over from last hospitalization, was dc'd this hospitalization, 
as there was no indication for patient to remain on it.

Chronic Diagnoses:
#. DM type II: Continued home insulin regimen: NPH 20U with 
breakfast and ISS.
.
#. GERD: Continued omeprazole per home regimen.
.
#. OSA: Patient had hypercapnic respiratory failure during last 
admission.  Was discharged on CPAP, has not been using at 
___.  Patient was prescribed CPAP in house and also 
given home O2 (2L).

#. Hx of atrial tachycardia.  Patient states this has not been a 
problem for years.  She follows with Dr. ___ has not 
seen him in years.  She has not been ablated.  She was continued 
on amiodarone per home regimen.

#. COPD: Patient denies hx of smoking, but has shortness of 
breath and wheezing responsive to nebs.  She has not had PFTs in 
our system.  She was continued on albuterol and ipratropium nebs 
prn SOB/wheezing, per home regimen.

#. Hyperlipidemia: Continued on simvastatin per home regimen.

#. Depression: continued paroxetine per home regimen.

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
Patient developed low grade temperature to 99.1F for two days 
prior to discharge, but no leukocytosis or obvious infectious 
symptoms. This temperature also is not a large increase from 
baseline body temperature of 98.9F. Additionally, blood cultures 
(some drawn from HD catheter site) were all no growth final, and 
CXR showed no pneumonia.  As patient had no obvious infectious 
symptoms, we felt she was safe for discharge with close 
follow-up at rehab and a low-threshold for further 
investigation. 
Due to a fever of 99.1F on the day of discharge, a set of 
surveillance blood cultures were drawn (on ___ which were no 
growth to date at the time of discharge.
Patient will also need INR monitoring/coumadin adjustment and 
hemodialysis at rehab.
